articles.title: Setting up prompt-scrub encryption without leaking the key
articles.focus: A practical guide to turning encryption on safely: why PROMPT_SCRUB_KEY=... inline is the wrong way, how read -rs and secret-manager export differ in their residual exposure (incl. /proc/<pid>/environ), and the TTY-detection rule that turns a piped invocation into a clean failure instead of a hang.

articles.title: The encrypted session envelope, annotated
articles.focus: A walk-through of the v1 envelope format and the reasoning behind each choice - AES-256-GCM over CBC, per-file random salt+IV, scrypt with N=16384/r=8/p=1 instead of PBKDF2, the KDF-param bounds check, the derived-key cache keyed by (passphrase, salt, params), and the write-side rule that prevents toggling encryptionEnabled from quietly rewriting an encrypted session in plaintext.

articles.title: Migrating plaintext sessions without locking yourself out
articles.focus: An operator-focused look at the prompt-scrub sessions encrypt path: why the command refuses to fabricate a session id that does not exist, why --rekey demands the OLD passphrase and never silently overwrites a file it cannot decrypt, what the encrypted/skipped/missing counts mean in the summary, and how the new SessionDecryptionError makes wrong-key and tampered-file cases distinguishable from genuinely expired sessions.
